svg.title: Why lasso sets coefficients to zero and ridge does not
svg.desc: Two panels in the plane of two coefficients, beta 1 and beta 2. In each, brown ellipses are contours of equal residual sum of squares around the least squares estimate. Left: the lasso constraint is a diamond with corners on the axes; the smallest ellipse that touches it meets it at the corner on the beta 1 axis, so beta 2 is exactly zero. Right: the ridge constraint is a circle with no corners; the ellipse touches it at a point where both coefficients are non-zero but smaller.

g.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: Ellipses: equal error (RSS) around the least squares estimate. Shaded: the coefficients the penalty allows (t = 1).
